title: Private endpoints and network isolation
description: Secure Azure PaaS services with private endpoints and virtual network integration. Understand private link, service endpoints, DNS zones, and how to build a zero-trust network boundary around your workloads.

data.text: By default, many Azure PaaS services expose public endpoints. Key Vault, Storage, and SQL Database all have public IP addresses that can be reached from anywhere on the internet—provided the caller has valid credentials. Private endpoints remove that public surface by mapping the service to a private IP address inside your virtual network.

Azure Private Link provides a private endpoint—a network interface inside your VNet—paired with a private link service on the provider side. Traffic stays within the Microsoft backbone network and never traverses the public internet. To the application, the service looks like any other resource in the same subnet.

terms.definition: A network interface in your VNet that maps to an Azure PaaS service over Private Link.
The provider-side abstraction that exposes a service through a private endpoint.
A VNet-level rule that extends the service's identity to your subnet, but traffic still routes over the Microsoft backbone, not a private IP.
A DNS zone that resolves the service's public name to the private endpoint IP.

cards.title: Service endpoint
cards.description: Adds your VNet subnet to the service's firewall allow list. Traffic still uses the service's public endpoint but is restricted to your subnet. Lower cost, slightly less isolation.

cards.title: Private endpoint
cards.description: Assigns a private IP from your VNet to the service. Traffic never touches the public endpoint. Stronger isolation, additional NIC and DNS costs.

data.title: DNS is the hidden dependency
data.text: A private endpoint works only if the client resolves the service name to the private IP. If your VNet does not use the private DNS zone, or if your custom DNS servers do not forward to Azure DNS, traffic may still attempt to reach the public endpoint.

data.title: Zero-trust network controls
items: Enable private endpoints for all PaaS services that support them.
Disable public network access on the service when private access is sufficient.
Use service endpoints only for services that do not yet support private endpoints.
Link private DNS zones automatically via the Azure portal or Bicep.
Validate connectivity with Azure Network Watcher IP flow verify.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Private endpoints remove public exposure by mapping services to private IPs.
Private Link is the underlying technology; private endpoint is the consumer resource.
DNS resolution must route to the private IP for the endpoint to be effective.
Combine private endpoints with RBAC for a defense-in-depth network strategy.
data.takeaway: Network isolation in Azure is not just firewalls—it is identity-aware connectivity from endpoint to DNS.
